articles.headline: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter's 2026 season: Snaps on offense, defense
articles.description: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
articles.headlineJa: ジャガーズのCB/WRトラビス・ハンターの2026年シーズンを追う：攻撃・守備でのスナップ数
articles.descriptionJa: 攻撃と守備の両方を担うこのコーナーバック兼レシーバーが、毎週どれだけのスナップ数を記録しているかを分析します。起用傾向に変化はあるでしょうか。
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. The Jaguars have followed through on that, making the 2025 No. 2 overall pick a starter on defense and mixing him in where designed on offense. 

He has started every game at cornerback and has played at least four snaps on offense in all but one game (Week 4 at Cincinnati). He has made big plays on both sides of the ball and had the best game of his career in Week 6, when he clearly showed what kind of threat he can be. Head coach Liam Coen has been consistent in saying that Hunter's offensive usage is fluid.

"You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches, then absolutely will."

How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game.

Week 10 at Tennessee Titans

Hunter came up with his highlight play of the season so far with a diving interception of a Cam Ward pass in the first quarter. Ward scrambled to his right on third-and-8 from the Jacksonville 35-yard line and threw back toward the left side of the field for receiver Elic Ayomanor near the sideline, but Hunter snagged the ball and cradled it to his body with his left hand as he hit the ground.

"It was an unbelievable catch, unbelievable play," head coach Liam Coen said. "... Such a special play by obviously a special player."

The Jaguars turned that into an eventual field goal and 10-3 lead early in the second quarter. Hunter, who is tied with cornerback Jourdan Lewis with a team-high three interceptions, played 56 snaps on defense, five on special teams, and five on offense against the Titans. He touched the ball on three of those offensive snaps: An end around that gained 3 yards and two catches for 16 yards.

Week 9 at Baltimore Ravens

It was a quiet night for Hunter on defense -- five tackles on 44 snaps -- but a bad one on offense. Hunter played six snaps on offense and fumbled the only time he touched the ball. Hunter caught a receiver screen from Trevor Lawrence, and Ravens safety Malaki Starks knocked the ball loose 1 yard behind the line of scrimmage. Linebacker Teddye Buchanan recovered the ball at midfield, and the Ravens took over with 5:10 to play in the third quarter with the Jaguars ahead 20-3.

The turnover didn't hurt the Jaguars, though, because the Ravens then turned the ball over on downs four plays later, with tight end Mark Andrews fumbling the snap on fourth-and-1. Hunter was officially credited with one catch for minus-1 yard.

Week 8 vs. Indianapolis Colts

Coming off a Week 7 bye week, it was a relatively quiet day from Hunter -- in terms of stats, anyway. Hunter played 49 of the 60 total snaps on defense tallying four tackles. He played six snaps on offense with one rush for 5 yards and no catches on one target

articles.headline: Week 10 winners and losers: McCaffrey, Gibbs and Mahomes dominate Sunday
articles.description: Christian McCafffrey, Jahmyr Gibbs and Patrick Mahomes put fantasy teams on their back in Week 10, while Jonathan Taylor and the Packers and Panthers' passing games had quiet days.
articles.headlineJa: 第10週の勝者と敗者：マッカフェリー、ギブス、マホームズが日曜を支配
articles.descriptionJa: 第10週ではクリスチャン・マッカフェリー、ジャマイア・ギブス、パトリック・マホームズがファンタジーチームを牽引した一方、ジョナサン・テイラー、そしてパッカーズとパンサーズのパスゲームは振るわなかった。
articles.body:
Week 10 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured huge games by Christian McCaffrey, Jahmyr Gibbs, Patrick Mahomes and rookie Emmett Johnson. Meanwhile, Jonathan Taylor, Trey McBride, as well as the Green Bay and Carolina passing games, underperformed in a big way Sunday.

So, who were the big winners and losers around the league? Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis.

Jump to a topic:

Ranking winners | Ranking losers 

Biggest injuries and what's next

Ranking fantasy winners of Week 10

1. Christian McCaffrey, RB, San Francisco 49ers

We have a new single-game high score for the season, as McCaffrey scored 46.3 fantasy points in a wild 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys. He was dynamic as a runner, but his receiving prowess in this game was extraordinary, as he had a career-high 32.1 points on catches. That's remarkable considering he has 121 games played and 12 games of 10-plus catches. By comparison, he had only four receptions in this game. The 49ers are doing a fine job keeping McCaffrey's 30-year-old legs fresh, though he does have two of his toughest matchups all season in the next two weeks (MIN, SEA). He's a clear RB1, but don't expect nearly the same ceiling for those games. -- Cockcroft

2. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions

After a quiet Week 9, Gibbs roared back with a 44.2-point performance in Munich, reminding us why he's the No. 1 player in our game. He tore up a New England Patriots defense that has been reeling the past two weeks; the Patriots surrendered a combined 80 points and 972 total yards to the Green Bay Packers and Lions.

Gibbs has exceeded 40 fantasy points in three of his past 16 regular-season games and 35-plus in seven of his past 20. His 253.4 points for the season is the eighth-most ever by a running back through his team's first nine games. Gibbs' Week 11 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers might seem scary -- they entered the week the No. 1 defense against running backs -- but he's on too historic of a run to quibble about his clear overall RB1 fantasy stock. -- Cockcroft

3. Patrick Mahomes, QB, Kansas City Chiefs

The deadline acquisition of WR Josh Downs paid immediate dividends for Mahomes and the Chiefs as the veteran quarterback scored 35.42 fantasy points (his most in a game in five years) and the team totaled 461 yards of offense. Kenneth Walker III's absence shifted the Chiefs' offensive philosophy more toward the pass, as fill-in running back Emmett Johnson has been excellent as a receiver.

Should Walker miss more time -- he's tentatively expected to play in Week 11 -- Mahomes could put up another big score in an extremely favorable matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. -- Cockcroft

4. Dak Prescott, QB, and George Pickens, WR, Dallas Cowboys

articles.description: We placed all 32 NFL teams into tiers based on their likelihood of making the playoffs, from Super Bowl favorites to the top draft pick candidates.
articles.headlineJa: NFLプレーオフ進出確率ティア：32チームの2026年ポストシーズン展望
articles.descriptionJa: スーパーボウル優勝候補からドラフト1位指名候補まで、プレーオフ進出の可能性に基づいて全32チームをティア分けしました。
articles.body:
The back half of the 2026 NFL season is upon us, and the playoff race is heating up. Though the standings tell us a lot about teams' chances to reach the postseason, they don't tell us everything. Team strength, injuries, tiebreakers, future strength of schedule and more can shift those odds up or down and don't show up in the win or loss columns.

So, ESPN analytics writer Seth Walder placed all 32 teams into eight tiers of playoff hopes, ranging from clear Super Bowl contenders to those already looking ahead to 2027. There is some fluidity in between because, for as confident as we feel about the league right now, things could look quite different once Week 18 rolls around. The tiers are based on information from ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI), betting lines, metrics, health status and some instinct.

Walder ranked the teams within each tier, too. All statistical rankings are through the Sunday late afternoon window unless otherwise indicated, and playoff chances are from the FPI.

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

Tier 1: True Super Bowl contenders

San Francisco 49ers (8-1)

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.8%

Chances to win the NFC West: 96.2%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 39.8%

Injuries have hit some of the 49ers' best players -- edge rusher Nick Bosa missed five games and wide receiver Mike Evans hasn't played since Week 6 -- but San Francisco is FPI's Super Bowl favorite for two main reasons. The Niners are basically a lock to reach the playoffs and a heavy favorite to win the NFC West given their current lead and head-to-head wins over the Rams and Seahawks. Brock Purdy entered Week 10 as the No. 1 quarterback in QBR and is arguably the league's MVP thus far. Kyle Shanahan might be the Coach of the Year thus far, too.

See remaining schedule

Buffalo Bills (8-1)

Chances to make the playoffs: >99.9%

Chances to win the AFC East: 99.7%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 31.0%

The Bills entered this season as the AFC favorite and nothing that's happened in the first 10 weeks has dispelled that notion. In fact, their hold on the conference looks even stronger now than it did then thanks to their conference-best record and the Ravens falling out of contention. The defense (16th in EPA per play) is still a concern, but quarterback Josh Allen, running back James Cook III and the Bills' offensive line does more than enough damage on offense.

Chances to make the playoffs: 99.9%

Chances to win the AFC South: 98.8%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 22.9%

articles.headline: Rockets blow out Wizards 147-119; hold Trae Young scoreless for first time in his career
articles.description: — Amen Thompson scored 26 points and Kevin Durant added 25 to help the Houston Rockets rout the Washington Wizards 147-119 on Sunday night for their fourth straight win.
articles.headlineJa: ロケッツがウィザーズを147-119で圧倒、トレ・ヤングをキャリア初の0得点に抑える
articles.descriptionJa: アーメン・トンプソンが26得点、ケビン・デュラントが25得点を挙げ、ヒューストン・ロケッツが日曜夜にワシントン・ウィザーズを147-119で撃破し、4連勝を飾りました。
articles.body:
WASHINGTON -- — Amen Thompson scored 26 points and Kevin Durant added 25 to help the Houston Rockets rout the Washington Wizards 147-119 on Sunday night for their fourth straight win.


              The Rockets also held Trae Young scoreless for the first time in his NBA career. He missed all five of his shots and had previous scored in all 511 of his prior career games with the Hawks and Wizards.


              Alperen Sengun added 19 points and eight assists and eight rebounds for the Rockets, who had a season-high for points. 


              Alex Sarr had 24 points and AJ Dybantsa added 16 for the Wizards. Dybantsa was 6-for-18 from the field. The Wizards have now lost seven games in a row after a 4-3 start to the season. Their last win came on Nov. 2 against the Magic.


              Washington went back-and-forth with Houston for the first quarter, but dominant second and third quarters by the Rockets paved the way for the blowout win. They outscored the Wizards 37-23 in the second and 46-34 in the third to pull away. Houston also outrebounded Washington 55-36.


              The Rockets used an 18-8 run to open the second half and put some distance between themselves and the Wizards. The lead eventually ballooned to as large as 31 points during that stretch. The Wizards were never able to keep pace with a Rockets offense that was efficient from the field and steadily grew their lead as the game wore on.


              Houston shot 56.5% from the field in the first half and made 10 of its 20 3-point attempts. Thompson, in the first two quarters, was 7 of 9 from the field and made each of his three 3-point attempts.


              Up next:
              Rockets: Visit the Miami Heat on Monday night.


              Wizards: Host the Memphis Grizzlies on Monday night.


              —-

articles.headline: Brunson hits tiebreaking 3-pointer in OT, Knicks earn 14th straight win over slumping Raptors
articles.description: — Jalen Brunson made a tiebreaking 3-pointer with 33 seconds remaining in overtime and the New York Knicks beat Toronto 112-108 on Sunday night, their 14th straight win over the Raptors.
articles.headlineJa: ブランソンがOTで勝ち越し3ポイントを成功、ニックスが不調のラプターズに14連勝
articles.descriptionJa: ジェイレン・ブランソンがオーバータイム残り33秒に勝ち越しの3ポイントシュートを決め、ニューヨーク・ニックスが日曜夜にトロントを112-108で撃破。ラプターズに対する14連勝を飾りました。
articles.body:
TORONTO -- — Jalen Brunson made a tiebreaking 3-pointer with 33 seconds remaining in overtime and the New York Knicks beat Toronto 112-108 on Sunday night, their 14th straight win over the Raptors.


              Brunson scored 28 points, and Karl-Anthony Towns had 28 points and 17 rebounds for the Knicks, who trailed by 13 points in the fourth quarter.


              Landry Shamet scored 23 points and OG Anunoby had 21 against his former team as the defending NBA champions snapped a two-game losing streak. 


              Scottie Barnes scored 30 points and Jamal Shead added 19 but the Raptors lost their fourth straight and seventh in nine.


              Toronto has led by double digits in each of its past three defeats. The Raptors couldn’t hold a 22-point lead against Boston on Wednesday, and blew a 17-point edge at Philadelphia on Thursday.


              Immanuel Quickley scored 17 points, RJ Barrett had 14 and Jakob Poeltl 11. Collin Murray-Boyles had a season-high 13 rebounds for the Raptors.


              Barnes returned after missing four games because of a strained left groin, but Toronto fell to 3-8 in 11 games without Kawhi Leonard, who remains sidelined because of a swollen left knee.


              The Raptors last beat New York nearly four years ago, a 125-116 home win on Jan. 22, 2023.


              The Raptors led 84-71 on Quickley’s 3-pointer with 8:55 remaining, but Shamet hit a tying 3 with 1:16 to play and Towns connected on a go-ahead 3 with 20 seconds left.


              Those were New York’s only two made 3-pointers on 10 attempts in the fourth quarter. The Knicks shot 1 for 7 from distance in the third.


              Barnes sent it to overtime by making a step-back 3-pointer with 13 seconds remaining.


              New York’s Josh Hart finished scoreless for the second consecutive game. Hart shot 0 for 5 in 26 minutes and came in only for defensive possessions in the fourth quarter and overtime.


              The teams meet in Toronto again on Tuesday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Aaron Donald savors first sack in 1,050 days, but Rams' win 'felt even better'
articles.description: Aaron Donald recorded his first sack since New Year's Eve in 2023 and helped the Rams top the Cardinals for their fourth straight win.
articles.headlineJa: アーロン・ドナルド、1,050日ぶりのサックに歓喜、それでもラムズの勝利は「さらに価値があった」
articles.descriptionJa: アーロン・ドナルドが2023年の大晦日以来となる初のサックを記録し、ラムズがカージナルスを破って4連勝を飾る原動力となりました。
articles.body:
PHOENIX -- When Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald brought down Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck in the second quarter, the veteran notched his first sack in 1,050 days.

That stretch included two seasons Donald spent in retirement before returning to the Rams in late August. Donald finished the game with 1.5 sacks, snapping an eight-game streak without a sack, which had been the longest drought of his career.

Though Donald said it felt "good" to get his first sack since New Year's Eve in 2023, he noted that it "felt even better that we won."

After starting 2-4, the Rams have won four games in a row.

With his 1.5 sacks on Sunday, Donald passed Justin Houston and Chandler Jones (112.0) for 31st on the NFL's all-time list. Donald also became the first player in franchise history age 35 or older to record more than one sack in a game.

"I'm never surprised," Rams coach Sean McVay said. "He never ceases to amaze me. I think the term '1 of 1' is thrown around way too loosely this day and age, but it's not with him. He's 1 of 1.

McVay added: "He's had a tremendous impact on this team. And it is certainly not exclusive to just getting a sack today. He's just made a tremendous impact, and he's a guy that everyone looks at and they say, watching the way that he moves, 'If we just mimic and emulate that, we'll be in good shape.'"

Donald and the Rams' defense held the Cardinals to just 123 yards and six first downs, both the fewest by any team this season, according to ESPN Research. The Rams did not allow a third-down conversion (0-for-6).

Donald said he feels good physically going into the Week 11 bye, especially after the Rams' defense played so few snaps Sunday.

"Get back right, get myself feeling 100% and get ready for this run," Donald said.

The Rams play the Green Bay Packers after the bye.

articles.headline: Spain 'overwhelmed' by 'exceptional' England: We also know how to lose
articles.description: Coach Luis de la Fuente said Spain were "overwhelmed" in the early stages of Sunday's 3-2 UEFA Nations League defeat to England, but backed his team to return stronger after seeing their three-year unbeaten run come to an end.
articles.body:
Coach Luis de la Fuente said Spain were "overwhelmed" in the early stages of Sunday's 3-2 UEFA Nations League defeat to England, but backed his team to return stronger after seeing their three-year unbeaten run come to an end.

Spain trailed 3-0 at the Metropolitano before goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams --- both created by Lamine Yamal -- saw them come close to pulling off a dramatic comeback.

The reigning world and European champions hadn't lost a competitive game in 43 matches, but now finish second behind England in their Nations League group, meaning a tougher draw for next year's quarterfinals.

"I take away only positives [from the game]," De la Fuente said in his postmatch news conference. "It highlights just how difficult it is to reach the level we've reached.

"Just as we know how to win, we also know how to lose. It's true that we were overwhelmed in the first 30 minutes, but I really believed we would mount a comeback in the final stages."

Spain had beaten England 3-2 at Wembley in their previous meeting in September. They will find out who they'll face in the next round of the Nations League in Friday's draw in Nyon, Switzerland.

"It's a shame we have to wait until March [to play again]," De la Fuente said on Sunday. "We'll like to have another game next week. But we'll head into that knockout tie with a real desire to win."

De la Fuente refused to be critical of his team, who were second-best to an exceptional England for the first 60 minutes.

"We faced an exceptional national team today," De la Fuente said. "It only underscores the value of everything we've achieved so far.

"I'm already looking forward to the next training camp. The team is motivated to take on a new challenge."

articles.headline: Andy Burnham urges caution on potential moves to scrap Premier League 3pm blackout
articles.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he would "urge caution" on scrapping the Saturday 3pm blackout.
articles.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he would "urge caution" on scrapping the Saturday 3pm blackout, and called for broadcasters to be mindful of the impact on fans caused by changes to kick-off times.

The ban on broadcasting live matches between 2.45 p.m. and 5.15 p.m on Saturdays was introduced in the 1960s but it could be dropped for the next set of Premier League, EFL and Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) rights cycles from 2029-30.

The purpose of the blackout has been to protect live attendance at matches, amid fears crowds would be affected, especially in lower league or non-league football, if top-flight matches were available to watch on television or streaming services.

Burnham said any decision to remove the ban would require careful thought about the consequences.

"I would urge a bit of caution on it [the blackout], because it does protect the income of lower league clubs," he said.

"If you have effectively wall-to-wall Premier League football at any time, it takes away perhaps the incentive to go and watch the football league or non-league.

"So I think it has to be considered carefully. I'm not going to take the pure consumer view here. I'll take the health of football approach to this particular issue.

"I would first of all want to protect the football pyramid before I agree to saying 'let's have even more live football."

- Andy Burnham to publish Man City mayoral dealings after intervention draws criticism

- UK PM Burnham wants 'outdated' football drinking ban scrapped

"I think it's about protecting the experience with the paying supporter, protecting the football pyramid. Those issues matter to me, first of all."

The trend in television rights has been to offer more matches in order to keep revenues up -- the current Premier League deal includes 270 live matches compared to 200 in the previous one for example.

The logical conclusion of that trend is for all matches to be made available live, and the SPFL's tender for its next set of rights is reported to offer the chance to do just that.

The blackout is enforced by article 48 of UEFA's statutes, which the Football Association and the Scottish Football Association choose to impose.

It applies when 50% or more of matches in the top two divisions are due to be played simultaneously.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters told talkSPORT in August that English football was leaning towards a blackout but added: "It's not just us involved in the decision about article 48. It's us, the EFL and the FA.

""We've got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change.

"It's not a decision for now. It's a decision we've got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do.

"I'd say in about 18 months time we'll come back to that decision about whether article 48 should remain or not."

articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂とニュース：ブルーノ・フェルナンデスはマンチェスター・ユナイテッドに留まるか？
articles.descriptionJa: 来夏に契約が切れるため、ブルーノ・フェルナンデスのマンチェスター・ユナイテッドでの将来は不透明であると報じられている。Transfer Talkが最新情報を伝える。
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now, while Arsenal are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now, says The Sun. Fernandes, 32, has a contract which expires next summer -- albeit with a one-year club option to renew -- and reportedly wants to wait to see what happens under new boss Mauricio Pochettino. The Portugal midfielder has been linked with a lucrative move to Saudi Arabia before.

- Arsenal are in the market for a center forward, and TEAMtalk claims that the Gunners are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. The 21-year-old joined Boro from Tottenham Hotspur this summer, after a loan spell at Oxford United in the Championship, and has hit the ground running, scoring 13 goals in as many appearances in the league so far. That has brought about plenty of transfer interest, but Middlesbrough will try to block any exit in January.

- Arsenal are continuing the push to sign a left-sided forward, with RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa leading their shortlist, says TEAMtalk. Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard left in the summer, and were replaced by Christos Tzolis before a move to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid fell short. With Mikel Arteta wanting more options on that flank, the report claims that talks have opened with Nusa's representatives about a possible switch, but the 21-year-old's transfer could cost €80 million.

- Tottenham defender Pedro Porro has decided that he only wants to join Barcelona if he leaves the club, according to Sport. The 27-year-old Spain right back has seen interest from the Blaugrana, as well as Real Madrid, despite only signing a new contract with Spurs in the summer. But while Barcelona are eyeing up a deal worth no more than €50 million next summer, Tottenham will stand firm on their €70 million valuation.

- AC Milan are looking to bolster in the forward areas during January, with Gazzetta dello Sport reporting that Real Madrid's Endrick and Club Brugge's Nicolò Tresoldi are on their shortlist. Endrick has seen few minutes in the starting XI for Los Blancos this season and Milan are keen on a loan deal with a permanent option included. Meanwhile, Tresoldi  22, who has five goals in four Champions League appearances this season, has caught the eye of a number of a teams and could move in a €60 million deal.

Other rumors

articles.headline: Reaction as Brazil legend Ronaldinho comes out of retirement at Ravenna
articles.description: Ronaldinho came out of retirement to play for Italian Serie C side Ravenna at age 46 in a bid to score his 300th career goal, but couldn't manage it. Here's what happened.
articles.headlineJa: ブラジルの伝説ロナウジーニョがラヴェンナで現役復帰、周囲の反応は？
articles.descriptionJa: ロナウジーニョはキャリア300ゴール目を達成するため、46歳でイタリア・セリエCのラヴェンナに加入し現役復帰したが、目標達成には至らなかった。その詳細をレポートする。
articles.body:
Former Barcelona and AC Milan forward Ronaldinho, 46, came out of retirement on Sunday to play for Italian Serie C club Ravenna against Forli, but could only play for 45 minutes.

The Brazil legend retired on 299 career goals, with his final match for Fluminense in September 2015, and he chose a third-tier club in Italy to try and reach the magic number of 300. However, despite a few neat flicks and tricks, he was unable to get on the scoresheet.

The 2002-World Cup champion and back-to-back FIFA World Player of the Year nearly got an assist when his corner found the head of Giulio Donati, but was well saved. And he played a small part in the opening goal as he held off an opponent before the ball found its way to Donati who unleashed a shot that former Brazil defender Roberto Carlos would have been proud of.

Catch up on everything that happened.

articles.headline: Haaland 'incredibly happy' at Man City, not thinking about possible sanctions
articles.description: Erling Haaland says he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City and his focus is on performing and not on the potential sanctions against the club.
articles.body:
Erling Haaland says he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City and his focus is on performing and not on the potential sanctions against the club.

City have appealed after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

The club could face heavy sanctions, including huge points deductions or demotion, should the verdict be upheld.

Haaland was asked about the case after Norway's 3-1 Nations League victory over Wales in Oslo on Saturday night, in which he scored his 66th goal in 60 international appearances.

"This is a question I struggle to answer, because it's a legal battle between the Premier League and Manchester City," Haaland told Norwegian broadcaster TV2.

"Am I supposed to answer that? I don't really know. It's a difficult question to answer when I don't know that much about it.

"To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022, and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024.

"I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player and I'm incredibly happy there."

Asked if the situation affects his City future, Haaland replied: "I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said I signed a long-term contract in 2024.

"I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

"I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

"I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1. Things aren't going so well in the Premier League, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham [on Saturday]."

- MrBeast, meet Haaland: Man City star puts YouTuber through soccer gauntlet

- Man City charges outcome cannot leave 'room for doubt' - sports integrity chief

City maintain they have a "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to support their case, despite being found guilty by an independent commission in September.

The commission's damning findings included breaches relating to the concealment of funding worth more than £830million over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

Haaland said the period under investigation happened before he joined City, and in the interview he painstakingly pointed out each stage of his football journey during that time.

He also name checked fellow Norwegian players Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen, Omar Elabdellaoui and Kjetil Haug, who spent time at City during that era.

Haaland said: "The investigation covered 2009-2018. I assume the answers will come.

"I don't know when. I haven't read much about it."

articles.headline: Arsenal's Bruno Guimarães: Learning a lot from 'machine' Declan Rice
articles.description: Bruno Guimarães has labelled Arsenal teammate Declan Rice a "machine" and said he's been learning a lot by playing alongside him.
articles.body:
Bruno Guimarães has labelled Arsenal teammate Declan Rice a "machine" and said he has been learning a lot by playing alongside him. 

The Brazil international joined Arsenal in the summer from Newcastle for £75 million ($101 million) and has made an impressive start to his career in north London. He has made 14 appearances in all competitions and scored two crucial goals in the Premier League against Sunderland and Leeds United. 

Guimarães has already shown signs of striking a good parternship with Rice in the middle of the park, and said their relationship extends beyond the field. 

"Look, I think that ever since he announced I was coming here, everything was practically set. He sent me a message right away saying: 'We've had a lot of fights in the past, but now we're friends -- we're going to play together. I'm really happy you're coming here. You're going to really raise the level of our team,'" he told ESPN Brazil. 

"So he was a guy who had already won me over even before I arrived. We know -- I'd say he's a complete player; he's a machine on the field. He can run, I don't know, 22 kilometers in a game without stopping for a second. I was really happy.

"I'm learning from him -- learning a lot from him -- since he's a very technical player. So, I think we have one of the best midfields in Europe here, yes -- given the number of players we have -- and anyway, I think Declan is a guy who's been helping me a lot; I felt right at home."

Guimarães joined Arsenal after five years at Newcastle, where he was the captain and beloved by the fanbase. He led the club to the 2025 Carabao Cup, their first domestic trophy in 70 years, and wrote himself into Newcastle's history books. 

So, leaving St. James' Park was "a very difficult decision" for him this summer. 

"I think I was one of the most beloved players during my time there, so it was a difficult decision, but in my mind, deep down, I felt I needed a new challenge. After almost five years at Newcastle, I think I'm driven by challenges and wanted a new one," he said.

- 'Extremely lucky' Declan Rice hints new Arsenal contract will be signed soon

- Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham's England record as youngest U21 player

"But, to be completely honest, it wasn't an easy decision. I had to think long and hard about it at the time. It was very difficult, too. Right after the World Cup, which was a very turbulent time -- so it was difficult for me in many ways. But in the end, I chose to make the move. I'm happy here; I'm starting my journey here as well.

"I think I'm increasingly understanding Arteta's approach -- which is completely different from what I was used to doing at Newcastle -- and I'm adapting more and more, getting to know the new players better. As I said, it's not easy to switch clubs after nearly five years, when you were already completely used to the routine, to everything. But I think this is a huge challenge, and I'm ready for it."

Information from ESPN Brazil's Artur Rocha,

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: Is Tottenham love affair finally over?
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino is back in the Premier League as the new Man United boss. For Tottenham fans, it's complicated.
articles.headlineJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマンUへ：トッテナムとの愛の物語はついに終わるのか？
articles.descriptionJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの新監督としてプレミアリーグに復帰します。トッテナムのファンにとっては、複雑な心境となるでしょう。
articles.body:
"He's magic, you know, Mauricio Pochettino!" For five years, these were the words that rang out amongst Tottenham fans.

First, at the old White Hart Lane -- a much-loved, if dilapidated, ground that became a fortress during Pochettino's years as head coach of the club. Then, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- a magnificent arena that, in recent years, has felt more like a house of horrors than any sort of stronghold.

But now Pochettino is back in the Premier League, this time as Manchester United manager. And for Tottenham fans who once dreamed of seeing the Argentine return to north London, it's another reminder that the man who gave us so many unforgettable memories might never be coming home.

The Pochettino love affair

The Argentine manager joined Tottenham in 2014 and was at the helm of one of the best, and most beloved, Spurs teams in the club's history. Under Pochettino, Harry Kane (now a Ballon d'Or winner!), Son Heung-Min, Christian Eriksen, Dele Alli, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Mousa Dembélé and Hugo Lloris all shone in ways that few football fans and pundits expected.

During the Pochettino era, Tottenham came agonisingly close to winning the Premier League and reached the Champions League final. They went an entire season unbeaten at home -- somewhat unthinkable now given the team's struggles at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- and played some of the most thrilling football in the league at the time.

There were famous victories over arch-rivals Arsenal and in Europe, including over Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund, and, of course, there was that night in Amsterdam. When Lucas Moura scored an astonishing hat trick against Ajax to send Spurs to the Champions League final for the first time in our history.

For many Spurs fans, including myself, the Poch years brought some of our best ever memories of supporting the club. There was a special connection between Pochettino and fans. He was revered and many of us hoped that it would last forever -- even if we all knew that, really, nothing ever lasts that long. Especially not in football.

When Pochettino was sacked, rather unceremoniously, in November 2019 -- just months after taking us to the Champions League final -- it felt somewhat unjust.

It was clear for anyone to see in 2019 that Tottenham's squad was beginning to get stale in a number of areas and that what the club truly needed was a rebuild. For myriad reasons, that never came to fruition and so, when, results on the pitch took a nosedive in the winter of that year the axe fell on Pochettino.

Overnight, the man who had turned Tottenham into a truly formidable side capable of beating anyone on their day was gone. Since then, it's fair to say that no other manager that has taken the wheel at the club has managed to form the same sort of bond that Pochettino had with us.

Many have come and gone but it hasn't yet felt like any of them have "got" us the way that Pochettino did. It is early days under Roberto De Zerbi

articles.headline: Every Manchester United player, manager, executive since Glazers' takeover: Where are they now?
articles.description: The Glazer family took over Manchester United in 2005, but what has happened to the players, managers and executive staff since?
articles.body:
Manchester United have shuffled from one crisis to another since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 after winning his 13th Premier League title.

The club were taken over in 2005 by American billionaires the Glazer family, but things have steadily unraveled under their leadership over the past 21 years and this season United have had their worst start to a Premier League season -- they sit just one point off the bottom of the table, having won once in 10 league games.

The finger of blame for United's woes has been pointed in many directions over the past decade or so, with the current hierarchy -- led by co-chairman Joel Glazer, minority owner Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox -- taking plenty of flak for the recent malaise.

But a lot of different backroom senior staff have been involved in the club since 2005, a lot of different managers have tried and failed, and a lot of players have come and gone. So where are they now?

Jump to: Backroom staff | Managers | Incoming players

Backroom staff

David Gill (CEO)

Gill left his role in the summer of 2013 and worked as vice president of UEFA and FIFA, as well as serving as a vice-chairman of the English Football Association. Still a Man United board member, Gill stepped down from his role on the UEFA executive committee in 2025 and was named the chair at Telix Pharmaceuticals in September 2026.

Ed Woodward (executive vice-chairman)

Having advised the Glazer family during the takeover of Manchester United, Woodward was hired in 2005 and given charge of the commercial and media operations two years later. He replaced Gill as CEO in 2013 and left the club in February 2022.

Now, he is the co-owner of the Quinta da Pedra Alta vineyard in Portugal. He is also a partner at AGILIS Sports Advisory Group -- a London-based mergers and acquisitions boutique focused on the sports sector -- a trustee at the Bloomsbury Football Foundation, and a non-exec board member at Sentient Sports, which describes itself as "pioneering AI-driven athlete protection and sports innovation."

Matt Judge (director of football negotiations)

The former investment banker joined the club in 2012 and was involved in United's transfer business from 2014. He led contract negotiations under Woodward from 2016, but he took up a new role in March 2021 when Darren Fletcher was named technical director and John Murtough was promoted to football director before leaving in 2022. He is now a partner, alongside Woodward, at the aforementioned AGILIS Sports Advisory Group.

Dan Ashworth (sporting director)

Ashworth was named the FA's director of elite development in 2012. He moved to Brighton to become the club's technical director in 2019, before joining Newcastle United as sporting director in 2022.
